opening.argument: The video opens by asking how Avalanche works and what distinguishes it, then explains its consensus process, chain architecture, and customizable subnets. Its staking discussion gives validator requirements and says rewards can be up to 7.65% annually; it does not promise a return or ask viewers to stake. The speakers also identify demand, competition, market volatility, and regulatory uncertainty as risks. These are features of an explanatory technology discussion, not a request for money, data, or participation in a transaction.

citations.quote: What is Avalanche. How does it work under the hood. What makes it stand out in the whole blockchain space?
Instead of one person deciding, each node on the network asks a small random handful of other people what they prefer.
each subnet defines its own rules its own virtual machine its own fee structure its own security model
You need to stake at least 2000 AVX, minimum two weeks, keep uptime around 80% mentioned. The rewards can be up to 7.65% annually

Also, lack of demand for the dApps built on it, fierce competition from other Layer 1s and Layer 2s, not generating enough fee revenue, general crypto market volatility and of course the ever present regulatory uncertainty.
